READ-ONLY investigation in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Do not modify anything.

I am refining a Jira story SFCC-743 "Product Card Group – PWA Component": a reusable component that renders an optional section header (title + link e.g. "Shop All") above a responsive row/grid of product cards. Props: display (3/4/6 cards), size (Desktop/Mobile/Tablet), showTitleAndLink, showLink, title, linkLabel. Used for "More from this category" and "Recommended for you" on PDP, plus PLP and Homepage.

Find whether any project requirement doc describes this. Specifically:

1. Read `.docs/prd/plp.md` and `.docs/prd/homepage.md` in full (or grep them heavily if very long). Look for ANY requirement about: a group/grid/carousel of N product cards, a section header with a title and a "shop all"/"view more" link, product recommendations sections, "more from this category", "recommended for you", "you may also like", editorial/product card rows.
   - Quote any matching requirement VERBATIM together with its requirement ID (the docs use IDs like SPR-NN, PRD-NN, DMU-NN, PLP-NN, HOME-NN — report whatever ID format actually appears).
   - If there is genuinely nothing matching, say so plainly and explicitly — do not stretch a loosely related requirement into a match.

2. Also check `.docs/prd/pdp.md` (if it exists) for "More from this category" / "Recommended for you" requirements, since the story names PDP as the primary usage. Same quoting rules.

3. List every file in `.docs/prd/` so I know what docs exist at all.

4. Grep the whole `.docs/` tree (case-insensitive) for: "product card group", "product-card-group", "card group", "shop all", "recommended for you", "more from this category". Report each hit with file path, line number, and the surrounding line quoted.

5. Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` for anything about Sprint 6, SFCC-743, product card group, or the PWA Kit Components epic (SFCC-2). Quote relevant lines.

6. Check whether `.docs/` contains any component-inventory or design-system doc that lists a "Product Card Group" — grep for "Component Inventory", "04.7", "component inventory".

Return a factual report with absolute file paths, line numbers, and verbatim quotes. If a doc does not exist, say so. Be precise about the difference between "no requirement exists" and "I could not find one".

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). ## Report: SFCC-743 "Product Card Group" vs project requirement docs

### Bottom line

**No requirement in `.docs/` describes this component.** Not in `plp.md`, not in `homepage.md`, not in `pdp.md`. There is no requirement anywhere in `.docs/` for a section header with a title + "Shop All"-style link above a configurable group of 3/4/6 product cards, and the literal labels in the story ("Shop All", "More from this category", "Recommended for you" on PDP) do not appear in any PRD. This is a definite absence, not a search failure — the PRD set is only 2,359 lines total and I read the three named docs in full plus grepped the whole tree.

The nearest *real* requirements are the PDP/Cart recommendation **carousels** (You May Also Like, Recently Viewed, Shop the Look) in `pdp.md` and `search.md`, and a "Recommended for You" carousel in **cart.md** (mini-cart, not PDP). Those are carousels, not a static N-card grid, and none of them specify a header link.

---

### 1. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/plp.md` (180 lines, read in full)

**No match.** PLP has no requirement for a product-card group with a title + link. It describes only the main category grid and adjacent editorial/link modules. Closest content, quoted verbatim so you can judge it yourself — I do not consider any of these a match:

- L13–15 (`SPR-01, SPR-02`):
  > - Dedicated category landing page; products displayed in a grid layout.
  > - "View more" pattern (not infinite scroll) loads additional products. The per-page count (currently 36) is handled in the FE — not configurable via BM (IC 2026-05-25).

  This is the paginated main grid, not a fixed 3/4/6-card group.

- L18 (`SPR-03, SPR-04`) — only PLP reference to recommendation modules, and only for vertical ordering:
  > - Editorial/SEO paragraph with a "read more" expand action (not collapsible — confirmed per 24.06 design review); positioned below YMAL / Recently Viewed (RJ note).

- L28–32 (`SPR-65, SPR-66`) — a row of **category text links**, not product cards:
  > - Configurable set of inline category links displayed below the hero image and above the product grid.
  > - Links are contextual — an edit of subcategories (not all are shown).

**"More from this category" does not appear. "Recommended for you" does not appear on PDP.** The confirmed PDP product-group modules are all described as **carousels**, §13 Content Modules:
